2036.subject: Zoology
2036.text:
Assertion : Pantothenic acid deficiency is probably the most common vitamin deficiency.
Reason : Macrocytic anaemia is a characteristic feature of pantothenic acid deficiency.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
2036.sol:
Pantothenic acid, (vitamin $\mathrm{B}_5$ ) formerly known as chick anti-dermatitis factor or filtrate factor is widely distributed in nature. It is a water soluble vitamin needed for metabolism of carbohydrates, fats and proteins. It is found in egg, cereals, legumes meat, etc. It is a surprise to biochemists that despite the involvement of pantothenic acid (as coenzyme A) in a great number of metabolic reactions, its deficiency manifestations have not been reported in humans, presumably because of the wide occurrence of this vitamin in almost all foods and because small amount can be synthesized in the body. Folic acid deficiency is probably the most common vitamin deficiency.
The macrocytic anaemia (abnormally large $\mathrm{RBC}$ ) associated with megaloblastic changes in bone marrow is a characteristic feature of folate deficiency.

2996.text:
At equilibrium for the reaction
$\mathrm{A}_2(g)+\mathrm{B}_2(g) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{AB}(g)$
the concentrations of $\mathrm{A}_2, \mathrm{ B}_2$ and AB respectively are $1.5 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{M}, 2.1 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{M}$ and $1.4 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{M}$ in a sealed vessel at 800 K. What will be $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}}$ for the decomposition of AB at same temperature?
2996.sol:
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{A}_2(\mathrm{ g})+\mathrm{B}_2(\mathrm{ g}) \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{AB}(\mathrm{ g}) \\
& \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}=\frac{[\mathrm{AB}]^2}{\left[\mathrm{ A}_2\right]\left[\mathrm{B}_2\right]} \\
& \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}=\frac{1.4 \times 10^{-3} \times 1.4 \times 10^{-3}}{1.5 \times 10^{-3} \times 2.1 \times 10^{-3}} \\
& \mathrm{ K}_{\mathrm{c}}=0.622 \\
& \mathrm{ K}_{\mathrm{p}}=\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}} \mathrm{x}(\mathrm{RT})^{\Delta \mathrm{n}} \\
& \Delta \mathrm{n}=0 \\
& \mathrm{ K}_{\mathrm{p}}=\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{c}}=0.622
\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{p}} \text{$ for $the decomposition of } \mathrm{AB}\left(\mathrm{ K}^{\prime}\right) & =\frac{1}{\mathrm{ K}_{\mathrm{p}}} \\
& =\frac{1}{0.622} \\
\mathrm{ K}^{\prime} & =1.60
\end{aligned}$

The oxides of the type \(\stackrel{+3}{E_2} $\mathrm{O}}_{3}\) of \($\mathrm{N}$\) and \( \mathrm{P}, \mathrm{P}$}_{2} $\mathrm{O}}_{3}\) \(\left(\mathrm{P}$}_{4} $\mathrm{O}}_{6}\right.\), dimer of \(\left.\mathrm{P}$}_{2} $\mathrm{O}}_{3}\right)\) are purely acidic, that of \($\mathrm{As}$\) \(\left(\mathrm{As}$}_{4} $\mathrm{O}}_{6}\right.\), dimer of \(\left.\mathrm{As}$}_{2} $\mathrm{O}}_{3}\right)\) and \( \mathrm{Sb}\left(\mathrm{Sb}$}_{4} $\mathrm{O}}_{6}\right.\), dimer of \(\left.\mathrm{Sb}$}_{2} $\mathrm{O}}_{3}\right)\) amphoteric and that of \( \mathrm{Bi}\left(\mathrm{Bi}$}_{2} $\mathrm{O}}_{3}\right)\) is predominantly basic.

6474.subject: Mathematics
6474.text: For what values of $m \in \mathbb{N}$, the following divisibility $x+y / x^m+y^m$ holds?
6474.sol:
Value of $m \in \mathbb{N}$ for which $x^m+y^m$ is divisible by $x+y$. Let $P(m)=x^m+y^m$ is divisible by $x+y$. Let us consider $m=1$. $P(1): x+y$ is divisible by $x+y ; \therefore P(1)$ is true
$\Rightarrow m=2 \Rightarrow P(2): x^2+y^2$ is divisible by $x+y$ which not true
$\Rightarrow P(2)$ is not true.
$\Rightarrow m=3 \Rightarrow P(3)=x^3+y^3$ is divisible by $x+y$.
$\therefore x^3+y^3=(x+y)\left(x^2-x y+y^2\right)\therefore P(3)$ is true.
Option 1 Even number wrong (m=2$ not valid).
Option 2 odd number right.
Option 3 All natural number wrong (\because m=2$ not valid)
Option 4 Only when $m=1$ wrong because valid for $m=3$ it is possible.

7043.text: If the angle between the circles $x^{2} + y^{2} + 4x - 5 = 0$ and $x^{2} + y^{2} + 2\lambday - 4 = 0$ is $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ then $\lambda =$
7043.sol:
$\text{The equation of the circles is given as,}$

$x^{2} + y^{2} + 4x - 5 = 0$

$x^{2} + y^{2} + 2\lambday - 4 = 0$

$\text{On comparing in equations with}x^{2} + y^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0$

${g}_{1} = 2, {f}_{1} = 0, {c}_{1} = - 5$

${g}_{2} = 0, {f}_{2} = \lambda, {c}_{2} = - 4$

$\text{The angle between the circles is,}$

$cos\theta = \dfrac{2{g}_{1}{g}_{2} + 2{f}_{1}{f}_{2} - {c}_{1} - {c}_{2}}{2\sqrt{{g}_{1}^{2} + {f}_{1}^{2} - {c}_{1}}\sqrt{{g}_{2}^{2} + {f}_{2}^{2} - {c}_{2}}}$

$cos\dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{2 \times 2 \times 0 + 2 \times 0 \times \lambda + 5 + 4}{2\sqrt{4 + 0 + 5}\sqrt{0 + {λ}^{2} + 4}}$

11868.text: The square of the distance from the origin to the point of intersection of the pair of lines $a x^2+2 h x y-a y^2+2 g x+2 \mathrm{fy}+\mathrm{c}=0$ is
11868.sol:
The equation of pair of lines is

a x²+2 h x y-a y²+2 g x+2 f y+c=0.....(i)

Let the lines represented by the given equation be

$\begin{aligned}$& l x+m y+n=0.....(ii) \\
& l^{\prime} x+m^{\prime} y+n^{\prime}=0.....(iii)
\end{aligned}

from eqs. (i), (ii) \& (iii)

$\begin{aligned}$& a x²+2 h x y-a y²+2 g x+2 f y+c=(l x+m y+n) \\
& $\left($l^{\prime} x+m^{\prime} y+n^{\prime}\right)
\end{aligned}

Equating the coefficients, we get

$\begin{aligned}$& $\mathrm{ll}^{\prime}=\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{mm}^{\prime}=-\mathrm{a}, \mathrm{nn}^{\prime}=\mathrm{c}$\\
& $\mathrm{mn}^{\prime}+\mathrmm^{\prime} \mathrm{n}=$2 $\mathrm{f}, \mathrm{nl}^{\prime}+\mathrmn^{\prime} \mathrm{l}=$2 $\mathrm{~g}, \mathrm{~lm}^{\prime}+\mathrm{ml}^{\prime}=$2 $\mathrm{~h}
\end{aligned}$Solving eqn. (ii) \& (iii) by cross multiplication:

$\frac{x}{m^{\prime}-m^{\prime} n}=\frac{y}{n^{\prime}-n^{\prime} 1}=\frac{1}{m^{\prime}-l m^{\prime}}$So, the point of intersection $\mathrm{P}$ is

$\left(\frac{m^{\prime}-m^{\prime} n}{m^{\prime}-l m^{\prime}}, \frac{n^{\prime}-n^{\prime} 1}{m^{\prime}-m^{\prime}}\right)$Square of distance from the origin

$\begin{aligned}$& =$\left(\frac{m n^{\prime}-m^{\prime} n}{m l^{\prime}-l m^{\prime}}\right)^$2+$\left(\frac{n l^{\prime}-n^{\prime} l}{m l^{\prime}-l m^{\prime}}\right)^$2 \\
& =$\frac{\left(m n^{\prime}-m^{\prime} n\right)^2+\left(n l^{\prime}-n^{\prime} l\right)^2}{\left(m l^{\prime}-l m^{\prime}\right)^2}$\\
& =$\frac{\left(m n^{\prime}+m^{\prime} n\right)^2-4 m m^{\prime} n n^{\prime}+\left(n l^{\prime}+n^{\prime} l\right)^2-4 n^{\prime} l^{\prime}}{\left(m l^{\prime}+l m^{\prime}\right)^2-4 m m^{\prime} l l^{\prime}}$\\
& =$\frac{4 f^2-4(-a) c+4 g^2-4 a c}{4 h^2-4 a(-a)}$\\
& =$\frac{f^2+g^2}{a^2+h^2}
\end{aligned}$

18908.text:
Inside a solenoid of radius 0.5 m , magnetic field is changing at a rate of $50 \times 10^{-6} \mathrm{ T} / \mathrm{s}$.
Acceleration of an electron placed at a distance of 0.3 m from axis of solenoid will be
18908.sol:
The changing magnetic field induce an electric field which will accelerate the electron.
The acceleration of electron will be
$a=\frac{e E}{m} \quad[\because F=q E]$
To find electric field $E$, we will use Faraday's electromagnetic induction.
$\mathrm{emf}, \varepsilon=\frac{-d \phi}{d t}(B \cdot A)$
where, $B$ is the magnetic field and $A$ is the area of cross-section.
$\varepsilon=-A \cdot \frac{d B}{d t}=-\pi r^2 \frac{d B}{d t}$
Now, electric field, $E=-\frac{\mathrm{emf}}{\text{ distance }}=-\frac{\dot{\varepsilon}}{d}=\frac{\pi r^2}{d} \frac{d B}{d t}$
Now, acceleration, $a=\frac{e}{m} \frac{\pi r^2}{d} \frac{d B}{d t}=\frac{1.6 \times 10^{-19}}{9.1 \times 10^{-31}} \times \frac{22}{7}\begin{aligned} & \times \frac{(0.5)^2}{(0.3)} \times 50 \times 10^{-6} \\ & =23 \times 10^6 \mathrm{ ms}^{-2}\end{aligned}$

20017.subject: Chemistry
20017.text: Identify the correct IUPAC name of $[\mathrm{CoCl}_2(\mathrm{NO}_2)(\mathrm{NH}_3)_3]$
20017.sol:
The coordination compound is $[CoCl_{2}(NO_{2})(NH_{3})_{3}]$.

First, determine the oxidation state of the central metal atom, Cobalt (Co). Let the oxidation state be $x$. The ligands are $Cl^{-}$ (charge -1), $NO_{2}^{-}$ (charge -1), and $NH_{3}$ (neutral, charge 0). The complex is neutral, so the sum of charges is zero: $x + 2(-1) + 1(-1) + 3(0) = 0$, which gives $x - 3 = 0$, so $x = +3$.

Next, name the ligands in alphabetical order. The ligands are ammine (NH_{3}$), chlorido (Cl^{-}$), and nitrito-N (NO_{2}^{-}$).

There are three ammine ligands, so use the prefix 'tri'. There are two chlorido ligands, so use the prefix 'di'. The ligand $NO_{2}$ is bonded through nitrogen, so it is named 'nitrito-N'.

Combining these, the alphabetical order is ammine, chlorido, nitrito-N. Thus, the name is triamminedichloridonitrito-N-cobalt(III).

Answer: Triamminedichloridonitrito- \mathrm{N}-\operatorname{cobalt}(\mathrm{III})$

20093.subject: Chemistry
20093.text: An aqueous solution of $X$ on addition of hydrogen peroxide in ice cold conditions gives blue colour to the ethereal layer. Then, $X$ can be
20093.sol:
The formation of a blue colour in the ethereal layer upon the addition of hydrogen peroxide (H_{2}O_{2}$) to an aqueous solution in ice-cold conditions is a characteristic test for the presence of chromium(VI).

When $H_{2}O_{2}$ reacts with acidified dichromate or chromate solutions, it forms chromium pentoxide (CrO_{5}$), which is blue in colour. The reaction is as follows:

$Cr_{2}O_{7}^{2-} + 2H^{+} + 4H_{2}O_{2} \rightarrow 2CrO_{5} + 5H_{2}O$

The $CrO_{5}$ species is unstable in aqueous solution and decomposes rapidly, but it is stabilized in ether, where it imparts a deep blue colour to the ethereal layer. Among the given options, acidified potassium chromate contains the chromate ion (CrO_{4}^{2-}$), which in acidic medium exists in equilibrium with the dichromate ion (Cr_{2}O_{7}^{2-}$), thus satisfying the condition for the test.

Answer: acidified potassium chromate

20126.subject: Chemistry
20126.text:
Identify the correct mathematical expression which represents the variation in molar conductivity of a weak acid having concentration C and ionisation constant $K_a$
(\lambda_m^\infty$ = molar conductivity at infinite dilution, \lambda_m$ = molar conductivity at concentration C)
20126.sol:
The degree of dissociation $\alpha$ for a weak electrolyte is given by:

$\alpha = \dfrac{\lambda_m}{\lambda_m^\infty}$

For a weak acid, the ionisation constant $K_a$ is given by Ostwald's dilution law:

$K_a = \dfrac{C \alpha^2}{1 - \alpha}$

Substituting the expression for $\alpha$ into the equation for $K_a$:

$K_a = \dfrac{C \left( \dfrac{\lambda_m}{\lambda_m^\infty} \right)^2}{1 - \dfrac{\lambda_m}{\lambda_m^\infty}}$

$K_a = \dfrac{C \dfrac{\lambda_m^2}{(\lambda_m^\infty)^2}}{\dfrac{\lambda_m^\infty - \lambda_m}{\lambda_m^\infty}}$

$K_a = \dfrac{C \lambda_m^2}{\lambda_m^\infty (\lambda_m^\infty - \lambda_m)}$

Answer: $K_a = \lambda_m^2 C / \lambda_m^\infty(\lambda_m^\infty - \lambda_m)$

20239.subject: Chemistry
20239.text: Which of the following compounds will show geometrical isomerism?
20239.sol:
Geometrical isomerism occurs in alkenes when each carbon atom of the double bond is attached to two different groups. Let us examine the structures of the given compounds.

For 2-methylbut-2-ene, the structure is $CH_3-C(CH_3)=CH-CH_3$. The carbon at position 2 is attached to two identical methyl groups. Therefore, it does not show geometrical isomerism.

For 1,2-dibromopropene, the structure is $CH_3-C(Br)=CH-Br$. The carbon at position 2 is attached to a methyl group and a bromine atom, which are different. The carbon at position 1 is attached to a hydrogen atom and a bromine atom, which are also different. Since both carbons of the double bond have two different groups attached, this compound exhibits geometrical isomerism (cis and trans forms).

For 1,1-diphenylethylene, the structure is $(C_6H_5)_2C=CH_2$. The carbon at position 1 is attached to two identical phenyl groups. Therefore, it does not show geometrical isomerism.

For 2-methylpropene, the structure is $(CH_3)_2C=CH_2$. The carbon at position 2 is attached to two identical methyl groups. Therefore, it does not show geometrical isomerism.

Answer: 1, 2-dibromopropene

20821.text: The correct condition for physical adsorption is
20821.sol:
Physical adsorption is an exothermic process, which can be represented by the equilibrium: Adsorbate + Adsorbent $\rightleftharpoons$ Adsorbed state + Heat.

According to Le Chatelier principle, for an exothermic process, a decrease in temperature favors the forward reaction, leading to increased adsorption.

Furthermore, increasing the pressure of the gas increases the concentration of gas molecules on the surface of the adsorbent, which also promotes physical adsorption.

Therefore, physical adsorption is favored by low temperature and high pressure.

Answer: Low $T$ and high $p$

21184.subject: Mathematics
21184.text: What is the argument of the complex number $\dfrac{(1+i)(2+i)}{3-i}$, where $i=\sqrt{-1}$ ?
21184.sol:
Let $z = \dfrac{(1+i)(2+i)}{3-i}$.

First, simplify the numerator:
$(1+i)(2+i) = 2 + i + 2i + i^{2} = 2 + 3i - 1 = 1 + 3i$.

Now, multiply the numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator $(3+i)$:
$z = \dfrac{(1+3i)(3+i)}{(3-i)(3+i)} = \dfrac{3 + i + 9i + 3i^{2}}{3^{2} + 1^{2}} = \dfrac{3 + 10i - 3}{9 + 1} = \dfrac{10i}{10} = i$.

The complex number $z = i$ can be written in polar form as $0 + 1i$.

The argument of $z = i$ is $\text{arg}(i) = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{2}$

21843.subject: Mathematics
21843.text: In how many ways can the word "CHRISTMAS" be arranged so that the letters '$\mathrm{C}$' and '$\mathrm{M}$' are never adjacent?
21843.sol:
The word CHRISTMAS contains 9 letters: C, H, R, I, S, T, M, A, S. The letter S repeats twice. The total number of arrangements is $\dfrac{9!}{2!}$.

To find the number of arrangements where C and M are never adjacent, we subtract the arrangements where C and M are adjacent from the total number of arrangements.

Treating (CM) as a single unit, we have 8 units: (CM), H, R, I, S, T, A, S. The number of arrangements of these 8 units is $\dfrac{8!}{2!}$. Since C and M can be arranged as CM or MC, we multiply by 2!.

Number of arrangements where C and M are adjacent = $\dfrac{8!}{2!} \times 2! = 8!$.

Number of arrangements where C and M are never adjacent = $\dfrac{9!}{2!} - 8! = \dfrac{9 \times 8!}{2} - 8! = 8! \times (\dfrac{9}{2} - 1) = 8! \times \dfrac{7}{2}$.

Answer: $8!\times \dfrac{7}{2}$

If $L_2$ is a line parallel to the vector $\vec{b} = \hat{j} + \hat{k}$,
Then the acute angle $\theta$ between the lines $L_1$ and $L_2$ is:
22164.sol:
The equation of line $M_1$ can be rewritten in standard form as:

$\dfrac{x-1}{1} = \dfrac{y-2}{-1} = \dfrac{z-5}{1}$

The direction vector of $M_1$ is $\vec{v}_1 = \hat{i} - \hat{j} + \hat{k}$.

The direction vector of $M_2$ is $\vec{v}_2 = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}$.

The line $L_1$ is the common perpendicular to $M_1$ and $M_2$. Its direction vector $\vec{d}_1$ is given by the cross product of $\vec{v}_1$ and $\vec{v}_2$:

$\vec{d}_1 = \vec{v}_1 \times \vec{v}_2 = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} \text{ and } \hat{j} \text{ and } \hat{k} \\ 1 \text{ and } -1 \text{ and } 1 \\ 1 \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } 1 \end{vmatrix}$

$\vec{d}_1 = \hat{i}(-1 - 2) - \hat{j}(1 - 1) + \hat{k}(2 - (-1)) = -3\hat{i} + 3\hat{k}$

We can take the simpler direction vector for $L_1$ as $\vec{d}_1 = -\hat{i} + \hat{k}$.

The line $L_2$ is parallel to $\vec{b} = \hat{j} + \hat{k}$, so its direction vector is $\vec{d}_2 = \hat{j} + \hat{k}$.

The acute angle $\theta$ between $L_1$ and $L_2$ is given by:

$\cos \theta = \dfrac{|\vec{d}_1 \cdot \vec{d}_2|}{|\vec{d}_1| |\vec{d}_2|}$

$\cos \theta = \dfrac{|(-1)(0) + (0)(1) + (1)(1)|}{\sqrt{(-1)^2 + 0^2 + 1^2} \sqrt{0^2 + 1^2 + 1^2}}$

$\cos \theta = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2} \times \sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$\theta = 60^{}^{\circ}$

Answer: $60^{}^{\circ}$

22806.text: Three point charges $-1 C,+1 C,+1 C$ are placed at points $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}, \mathrm{C}$ respectively of a triangle ABC. What is the total potential energy of the system? [given $\mathrm{AB}=\mathrm{AC}=6 \mathrm{ cm}$ and $\mathrm{BC}=3 \mathrm{ cm}$ ]
22806.sol:
The potential energy $U$ of a system of point charges is given by the sum of the potential energies of all pairs of charges: $U = k \left( \dfrac{q_A q_B}{r_{AB}} + \dfrac{q_B q_C}{r_{BC}} + \dfrac{q_A q_C}{r_{AC}} \right), where $ k = 9 $\times10^9 \text{ N m}^2 \text{ C}^{-2}.

Given charges are $ q_A = -1 $\text{ C}, $ q_B = +1 $\text{ C}, $ q_C = +1 $\text{ C}.

Given distances are $ r_{AB} = 6 $\text{ cm} =0.06 \text{ m}, $ r_{AC} = 6 $\text{ cm} =0.06 \text{ m}, and $ r_{BC} = 3 $\text{ cm} =0.03 \text{ m}.

Substituting the values into the formula:

$ U = 9 $\times10^9 \left( \dfrac{(-1)(1)}{0.06} + \dfrac{(1)(1)}{0.03} + \dfrac{(-1)(1)}{0.06} \right)$

$U = 9 \times 10^9 \left( -\dfrac{1}{0.06} + \dfrac{1}{0.03} - \dfrac{1}{0.06} \right)<$ br>
$U = 9 \times10^9 \left( -\dfrac{2}{0.06} + \dfrac{1}{0.03} \right)$

$U = 9 \times 10^9 \left( -\dfrac{1}{0.03} + \dfrac{1}{0.03} \right)<$br>
$U = 9 \times10^9 \times0 = 0 \text{ J}.$

Answer: 0 J (Zero joule)

22907.subject: Physics
22907.text:
A planet has double the mass of the earth and double the radius. The gravitational potential at the surface of the Earth is $\mathrm{V}$ and the magnitude of the gravitational field strength is $\mathrm{g}$. The gravitational potential and gravitational field strength on the surface of the planet are
No.PotentialField
AV$\dfrac{g}{4}$
B2V$\dfrac{g}{2}$
CV$\dfrac{g}{2}$
D2V$\dfrac{g}{4}$
22907.sol:
The gravitational potential $V$ at the surface of a planet of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is given by $V = -\dfrac{GM}{R}$.

The gravitational field strength $g$ at the surface is given by $g = \dfrac{GM}{R^2}$.

For the Earth, $V_E = -\dfrac{GM_E}{R_E} = V$ and $g_E = \dfrac{GM_E}{R_E^2} = g$.

For the given planet, $M_P = 2M_E$ and $R_P = 2R_E$.

The gravitational potential at the surface of the planet is $V_P = -\dfrac{GM_P}{R_P} = -\dfrac{G(2M_E)}{2R_E} = -\dfrac{GM_E}{R_E} = V$.

The gravitational field strength at the surface of the planet is $g_P = \dfrac{GM_P}{R_P^2} = \dfrac{G(2M_E)}{(2R_E)^2} = \dfrac{2GM_E}{4R_E^2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \dfrac{GM_E}{R_E^2} \right) = \dfrac{g}{2}$.

Answer: C

23005.subject: Physics
23005.text: A bar magnet is suspended in a uniform magnetic field of field strength 0.36 T. If the magnetic moment of the bar magnet is $4 \mathrm{Am}^2$ then the work done in rotating the magnet from its most stable position to its most unstable position is:
23005.sol:
The potential energy $U$ of a magnetic dipole with magnetic moment $\vec{M}$ in a uniform magnetic field $\vec{B}$ is given by $U = -\vec{M} \cdot \vec{B} = -MB \cos \theta$, where $\theta$ is the angle between $\vec{M}$ and $\vec{B}$.

The most stable position corresponds to $\theta = 0^{{}^{\circ}}$, where $U_{initial} = -MB \cos(0^{{}^{\circ}}) = -MB$.

The most unstable position corresponds to $\theta = 180^{{}^{\circ}}$, where $U_{final} = -MB \cos(180^{{}^{\circ}}) = MB$.

The work done $W$ in rotating the magnet is the change in potential energy: $W = U_{final} - U_{initial} = MB - (-MB) = 2MB$.

Given $M = 4 \text{ Am}^2$ and $B = 0.36 \text{ T}$, we have $W = 2 \times 4 \times 0.36 = 8 \times 0.36 = 2.88 \text{ J}$.

Answer: 2.88 J

23092.subject: Physics
23092.text: If $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$ be the apparent angles of dip observed in two vertical planes at right angles to each other, then the true angle of $\operatorname{dip} \theta$ is given by
23092.sol:
Let $B$ be the total intensity of the Earth's magnetic field, $B_H$ be the horizontal component, and $B_V$ be the vertical component. The true angle of dip $\theta$ is given by $\tan \theta = \dfrac{B_V}{B_H}$.

Consider two vertical planes at right angles to each other. Let the horizontal component $B_H$ make an angle $\alpha$ with the first plane. Then the horizontal components in the two planes are $B_H \cos \alpha$ and $B_H \sin \alpha$.

The apparent angles of dip $\theta_1$ and $\theta_2$ in these two planes are given by $\tan \theta_1 = \dfrac{B_V}{B_H \cos \alpha}$ and $\tan \theta_2 = \dfrac{B_V}{B_H \sin \alpha}$.

Taking the reciprocals, we have $\cot \theta_1 = \dfrac{B_H \cos \alpha}{B_V} = \dfrac{1}{\tan \theta} \cos \alpha$ and $\cot \theta_2 = \dfrac{B_H \sin \alpha}{B_V} = \dfrac{1}{\tan \theta} \sin \alpha$.

Squaring and adding these equations, we get $\cot^2 \theta_1 + \cot^2 \theta_2 = \dfrac{1}{\tan^2 \theta} (\cos^2 \alpha + \sin^2 \alpha) = \cot^2 \theta$.

Answer: $\cot ^2 \theta=\cot ^2 \theta_1+\cot ^2 \theta_2$

23239.text: A ball is moving in a circular path of radius $5 \mathrm{ m}$. If tangential acceleration at any instant is $10 \mathrm{ ms}^{-2}$ and the net acceleration makes an angle of $30^{{}^{\circ}}$ with the centripetal acceleration, then, the instantaneous speed is
23239.sol:
The tangential acceleration is given as $a_t = 10 \mathrm{ ms}^{-2}$.

The centripetal acceleration is given by $a_c = \dfrac{v^2}{r}$, where $v$ is the instantaneous speed and $r = 5 \mathrm{ m}$. Thus, $a_c = \dfrac{v^2}{5}$.

The net acceleration $\vec{a}$ is the vector sum of the tangential acceleration $\vec{a}_t$ and the centripetal acceleration $\vec{a}_c$. Since $\vec{a}_t$ and $\vec{a}_c$ are perpendicular, the angle $\theta$ between the net acceleration $\vec{a}$ and the centripetal acceleration $\vec{a}_c$ is given by $\tan \theta = \dfrac{a_t}{a_c}$.

Given $\theta = 30^{{}^{\circ}}$, we have $\tan 30^{{}^{\circ}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$.

Substituting the values, $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}} = \dfrac{10}{v^2 / 5} = \dfrac{50}{v^2}$.

Therefore, $v^2 = 50 \sqrt{3}$.

Calculating the value, $v^2 = 50 \times 1.732 = 86.6$.

$v = \sqrt{86.6} \approx 9.3 \mathrm{ ms}^{-1}$.

Answer: $9.3 \mathrm{ ms}^{-1}$

23312.text:
Force constant of interatomic bond, in a certain element, is $7.1\ Nm^{-1}$. If the atom oscillates in SHM in a certain direction, what is its frequency?
Given: Mole weight of the given element is 108g and Avagadro's number $= 6.023 \times 10^{23}\ g\ mol^{-1}$
23312.sol:
Mass of a single atom is given by $m = \dfrac{M}{N_A}$

Substituting the given values:

$m = \dfrac{108 imes 10^{-3}}{6.023 imes 10^{23}} \approx 1.793 imes 10^{-25}\ kg$

The frequency of oscillation of the atom in simple harmonic motion is given by:

$ u = \dfrac{1}{2\pi} \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}$

Substituting $k = 7.1\ N\ m^{-1}$ and $m = 1.793 imes 10^{-25}\ kg$:

$ u = \dfrac{1}{2\pi} \sqrt{\dfrac{7.1}{1.793 imes 10^{-25}}}$

$ u = \dfrac{1}{2\pi} \sqrt{39.6 imes 10^{24}}$

$ u = \dfrac{6.29 imes 10^{12}}{2\pi} \approx 1 imes 10^{12}\ s^{-1}$

Answer: $1 imes 10^{12}\ s^{-1}$

23326.sol:
The function $y = \log(\omega t)$ is defined for $\omega t > 0$.

A function $f(t)$ is periodic if there exists a positive constant $T$ such that $f(t + T) = f(t)$ for all $t$.

For the given function, $\log(\omega(t + T)) = \log(\omega t + \omega T) = \log(\omega t) + \log(1 + \dfrac{T}{t})$.

Since $\log(1 + \dfrac{T}{t}) \neq 0$ for any $T > 0$ and $t > 0$, the condition $f(t + T) = f(t)$ cannot be satisfied for any constant $T$.

Therefore, the function $y = \log(\omega t)$ is a non-periodic function.

Answer: non-periodic function

24592.text: For a first-order reaction $\text{R} \longrightarrow \text{P}$ at a given temperature, $k$ is the rate constant. For this reaction, at the given temperature, the concentrations of $\text{R}$ and $\text{P}$ at a time $t$ are $[\text{R}]$ and $[\text{P}]$, respectively. The correct graphical representation(s) for this reaction is(are)
24592.sol:
For a first-order reaction $\text{R} \rightarrow \text{P}$, the rate law is given by:

$-\dfrac{\text{d}[\text{R}]}{\text{d}t} = \dfrac{\text{d}[\text{P}]}{\text{d}t} = k[\text{R}]$

Integrating this, the concentration of the reactant at time $t$ is $[\text{R}] = [\text{R}]_0 e^{-kt}$.

The concentration of the product at time $t$ is $[\text{P}] = [\text{R}]_0 - [\text{R}] = [\text{R}]_0 (1 - e^{-kt})$.

The plot of $[\text{P}]$ versus $t$ follows the equation $[\text{P}] = [\text{R}]_0 (1 - e^{-kt})$. This represents a curve that starts from the origin and is concave down, approaching a constant value $[\text{R}]_0$. The graph in (A) is concave up, making it incorrect.

The plot of $\dfrac{\text{d}[\text{R}]}{\text{d}t}$ versus $[\text{R}]$ follows the equation $\dfrac{\text{d}[\text{R}]}{\text{d}t} = -k[\text{R}]$. This is a straight line passing through the origin with a negative slope ($-k$). The graph in (B) has a positive slope, making it incorrect.

The plot of $\dfrac{\text{d}[\text{P}]}{\text{d}t}$ versus $t$ follows the equation $\dfrac{\text{d}[\text{P}]}{\text{d}t} = k[\text{R}]_0 e^{-kt}$. This represents an exponentially decreasing curve with respect to time. The graph in (C) matches this behavior, making it correct.

The rate constant $k$ depends only on the temperature and is independent of time. Therefore, the plot of $k$ versus $t$ is a horizontal straight line. The graph in (D) matches this, making it correct.

Answer: ;

$P\left(\text{Blue from Box}I\right) = \dfrac{3}{16}$

26008.text:
A series LCR circuit is connected to a $45sin ( \omegat )$ Volt source. The resonant angular frequency of the circuit is ${10}^{5}rad{s}^{- 1}$ and current amplitude at resonance is ${I}_{0}$. When the angular frequency of the source is $\omega = 8 \times {10}^{4}rad{s}^{- 1}$, the current amplitude in the circuit is $0 . 05{I}_{0}$. If $L = 50mH$, match each entry in List-$I$ with an appropriate value from List-$II$ and choose the correct option.

List-$I$ List-$II$
$P$ ${I}_{0}$ in $mA$ $1$ $44 . 4$
$Q$ The quality factor of the circuit $2$ $18$
$R$ The bandwidth of the circuit in $rad{s}^{- 1}$ $3$ $400$
$S$ The peak power dissipated at resonance in Watt $4$ $2250$
$5$ $500$
26008.sol:
Resonant angular frequency is given by, $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{LC}} = {10}^{5}$

$\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{\left(50 \times {10}^{- 3}\right)C}} = {10}^{5} ⇒ C = 2 \times {10}^{- 9}F$

Given: $V = 45sin\left(\omegat\right)$. Therefore, ${V}_{0} = 45$.

Now, ${I}_{0} = \dfrac{{V}_{0}}{R} = \dfrac{45}{R} . . . \left(ii\right)$

Inductive reactance, ${X}_{L} = \omegaL = \left(8 \times {10}^{4}\right) \times \left(50 \times {10}^{- 3}\right) = 4000Ω$.

and capacitive reactance, ${X}_{C} = \dfrac{1}{\omegaC} = \dfrac{1}{\left(8 \times {10}^{4}\right) \times \left(2 \times {10}^{- 9}\right)} = 6250Ω$.

For new current amplitude, we can write

$0 . 05{I}_{0} = \dfrac{45}{\sqrt{{R}^{2} + {\left({X}_{L} - {X}_{C}\right)}^{2}}} ⇒ 0 . 05{I}_{0} = \dfrac{45}{\sqrt{{R}^{2} + {\left(6250 - 4000\right)}^{2}}} ⇒ 0 . 05 \times \dfrac{45}{R} = \dfrac{45}{\sqrt{{R}^{2} + {\left(6250 - 4000\right)}^{2}}} ⇒ {R}^{2} + {\left(6250 - 4000\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{{R}^{2}}{{\left(0 . 05\right)}^{2}} ⇒ {R}^{2} + {\left(2250\right)}^{2} = 400{R}^{2} ⇒ R = \dfrac{2250}{\sqrt{399}} = 112 . 67Ω$

Where ${X}_{{L}_{0}} = {X}_{{C}_{0}}$ are at resonant frequencies

On solving, $⇒ {I}_{0} = \dfrac{45}{R} ≃ 400mA$

Quality factor $Q = \dfrac{{X}_{L}}{R} ≃ 44 . 44$

Now, $Q = \dfrac{{\omega}_{0}}{∆ \omega} ⇒ ∆ \omega ≃ 2250rad{s}^{- 1}$.

Peak power $= 45 \times \dfrac{400}{1000}W = 18W$

Therefore, $P \to 3, Q \to 1, R \to 4, S \to 2$.

26523.text: A rod of length $2cm$ makes an angle $\dfrac{2π}{3}rad$ with the principal axis of a thin convex lens. The lens has a focal length of $10cm$ and is placed at a distance of $\dfrac{40}{3}cm$ from the object as shown in the figure. The height of the image is $\dfrac{30\sqrt{3}}{13}cm$ and the angle made by it with respect to the principal axis is $\alpha$ rad. The value of $α$ is $\dfrac{π}{n}rad$, where $n$ is
26523.sol:
In convex lens, when an object is placed in between the centre of curvature and focus, the real image is formed behind the centre of curvature. The size of the image is larger than that of the object.

Here, the angle made by inner side of rod with principal axis is $\pi - \dfrac{2\pi}{3} = \dfrac{\pi}{3}rad$.

From figure, height of object is ${h}_{o} = 2sin60 ° = 2 \times \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = \sqrt{3}cm$ and given height of image ${h}_{i} = \dfrac{30\sqrt{3}}{13}cm$

Size of object is $u = \dfrac{40}{3} + 1 = \dfrac{43}{3}cm$

Now, using lens equation, $\dfrac{1}{v} - \dfrac{1}{- u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

$⇒ v = \dfrac{fu}{f - u}$

Image distance, $O{A}^{'} = \dfrac{\dfrac{40}{3} \times 10}{\dfrac{43}{3} - 10} = 40cm$

And $O{B}^{'} = \dfrac{\dfrac{43}{3} \times 10}{\dfrac{43}{3} - 10} = \dfrac{430}{13}cm$

$∴ {A}^{'}{B}^{'} = 40 - \dfrac{430}{13} = \dfrac{90}{13}cm$

$∴ tan\alpha = \dfrac{30\sqrt{3}}{13 \times \left(\dfrac{90}{13}\right)} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

$⇒ \alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

$∴ n = 6 . 00$

31124.text: The number of $P - OH$ bonds and the oxidation state of phosphorus atom in pyrophosphoric acid $\left({H}_{4}{P}_{2}{O}_{7}\right)$, respectively are:
31124.sol:
As we can clearly see in the structure,

the number of $P - OH$ bonds is 4.

The oxygen is an electronegative element and will always carry a negative charge. Now, it depends on its surrounding atoms about what charge it carries. In case of a hydroxyl group, the hydrogen carries a +1 charge. So, the opposite charge generated on the oxygen atom along with magnitude will be -1.
In the case of only oxygen atoms, we know that the oxidation number of oxygen is equal to -2. So, the charge generated on the adjacent atom of oxygen will be +2.
Thus, the oxidation state of phosphorus atom will be generated because of:
Oxidation state on phosphorous $= [ 2 \times ( P - OH ) + ( 1 \times = O ) + ( 1 \times - O ) ]$ oxidation states

Thus, the oxidation state of both the phosphorus atoms will be:
${P}_{O . S} = 2 \times ( + 1 ) + 1 \times ( + 2 ) + 1 \times ( + 1 ) = + 5$

32913.subject: Mathematics
32913.text:
Let $A = \left[{a}_{ij}\right]$ be a $3 \times 3$ matrix, where ${a}_{ij} = \left\{\begin{cases}1 & , & ifi = j \\ - x & , & if\left|i - j\right| = 1 \\ 2x + 1 & , & otherwise\end{cases}\right)
Let a function $f: R \to R$ be defined as $f\left(x\right) = det \left(A\right)$. Then the sum of maximum and minimum values of $f$ on $R$ is equal to:
32913.sol:
We have,

${a}_{ij} = \left\{\begin{cases}1 & , & ifi = j \\ - x & , & if\left|i - j\right| = 1 \\ 2x + 1 & , & otherwise\end{cases}\right)

Then,

$A = \left[\begin{cases}1 & - x & 2x + 1 \\ - x & 1 & - x \\ 2x + 1 & - x & 1\end{cases}\right]$

$⇒ \left|A\right| = \left(1 - {x}^{2}\right) + x\left(- x + 2{x}^{2} + x\right) + \left(2x + 1\right)\left({x}^{2} - 2x - 1\right)$

$⇒ \left|A\right| = 1 - {x}^{2} + 2{x}^{3} + \left(2{x}^{3} - 4{x}^{2} - 2x\right) + \left({x}^{2} - 2x - 1\right)$

$⇒ \left|A\right| = f\left(x\right) = 4{x}^{3} - 4{x}^{2} - 4x$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = 4\left(3{x}^{2} - 2x - 1\right)$

For maxima or minima, ${f}^{'}\left(x\right) = 0$

$⇒ 3{x}^{2} - 2x - 1 = 0$

$⇒ x = 1, \dfrac{- 1}{3}$

Now,

${f}^{' '}\left(x\right) = 4\left(6x - 2\right)$

${f}^{' '}\left(1\right) = 4\left(6 \cdot 1 - 2\right) = 16 > 0$( point of minima)

${f}^{' '}\left(- \dfrac{1}{3}\right) = 4\left(6 \cdot \left(- \dfrac{1}{3}\right) - 2\right) = - 16 < 0$ ( point of maxima)

Hence, required sum is

$f\left(1\right) + f\left(- \dfrac{1}{3}\right)$

$= - 4 + \dfrac{20}{27} = - \dfrac{88}{27}$

$\operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{z-1}{2 z+\mathrm{i}}\right)+\operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{\bar{z}-1}{2 \bar{z}-\mathrm{i}}\right)=2$
is a circle of radius $r$ and center $(a, b)$ then $\frac{15 a b}{r^2}$ is equal to :
33763.sol:
$\begin{aligned}& \operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{z-1}{2 z+i}\right)+\operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{\bar{z}-1}{2 \bar{z}-i}\right)=2 \\
& \text{ Here, } \frac{z-1}{2 z+i}=\left(\frac{\overline{\bar{z}-1}}{2 \bar{z}-i}\right)=2 \\
& =\operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{z-1}{2 z+i}\right)+\operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{\mathrm{z}-1}{2 z+i}\right)=2 \\
& =2 \operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{z-1}{2 z+1}\right)=2 \Rightarrow \operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{z-1}{2 z+i}\right)=1\end{aligned}$Let $z=x+i y \begin{aligned}& \operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{(x-1)+i y}{2 x+i(2 y+1)}\right)=1 \Rightarrow \operatorname{Re}\left[\frac{((x-1)+i y)(2 x-i(y+1)}{(2 x+i(2 y+1)(2 x-i(2 y+1))}\right]=1 \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{2 x(x-1)+y(2 y+1)}{4 x^2+(2 y+1)^2}=1 \\
& \Rightarrow 2 x^2-2 x+2 y^2+y=4 x^2+4 y^2+1+4 y \\
& \Rightarrow 2 x^2+2 y^2+3 y+2 x+1=0 \\
& \Rightarrow x^2+y^2+x+\frac{3}{2} y+\frac{1}{2}=0 \\
& \text{ centre }=\left(\frac{-1}{2}, \frac{-3}{4}\right), r=\sqrt{\frac{1}{4}+\frac{9}{16}-\frac{1}{2}}=\frac{\sqrt{5}}{4} \\
& a=\frac{-1}{2}, b=\frac{-3}{4}, r^2=\frac{5}{16} \\
& 15 \frac{a b}{r^2}=15 \times\left(\frac{-1}{2}\right) \times\left(\frac{-3}{4}\right) \times \frac{16}{5}=18\end{aligned}$

33814.sol:

Now on comparing real and imaginary part, we get

Now solving,

$⇒ {\alpha}^{2} + 4\alpha + 20 = {\alpha}^{2} + 8\alpha + 16$

$⇒ \alpha = 1$

We know that quadratic equation is given by,

${x}^{2} - \left(\text{sum of roots}\right)x + \left(\text{product of roots}\right) = 0$

Let $f, g: R \to R$ be functions defined by
$f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}\left[x\right] & , x < 0 \\ \left|1 - x\right| & , x \ge 0\end{cases}\right) and
$g\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}{e}^{x} - x, & x < 0 \\ {\left(x - 1\right)}^{2} - 1, & x \ge 0\end{cases}\right)
where $\left[x\right]$ denote the greatest integer less than or equal to $x$. Then, the function fog is discontinuous at exactly
34026.sol:
Let $f, g: R \to R$ be functions defined by
$f\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}\left[x\right] & , x < 0 \\ \left|1 - x\right| & , x \ge 0\end{cases}\right) and
$g\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{cases}{e}^{x} - x, & x < 0 \\ {\left(x - 1\right)}^{2} - 1, & x \ge 0\end{cases}\right)

$⇒ fog\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{array}{ll}\left[g\left(x\right)\right], g\left(x\right) < 0 \\ \left|1 - g\left(x\right)\right|, g\left(x\right) \ge 0\end{array}\right)

After taking intersection we get,

$⇒ fog\left(x\right) = \left\{\begin{array}{ll}\left|1 + x - {e}^{x}\right|, x < 0 \\ \left[{\left(x - 1\right)}^{2}\right] - 1, 0 \le x < 2 \\ \left|2 - {\left(x - 1\right)}^{2}\right|, x \ge 2\end{array}\right)

Now, checking continuity at $x = 0$ and at $x = 2$

We get, $fog\left({0}^{+}\right) = - 1$, $fog\left(0\right) = 0$

Hence, discontinuous at $x = 0$

And, $fog\left({2}^{+}\right) = 1$, $fog\left({2}^{-}\right) = - 1$

Hence, discontinuous at $x = 2$

36344.sol:
For $6^m + 9^n \equiv 0 \pmod{5}$:
$6 \equiv 1 \pmod{5}$ and $9 \equiv -1 \pmod{5}$
So $6^m + 9^n \equiv 1 + (-1)^n \pmod{5}$
This equals 0 only when n is odd.
Number of odd n in {1,...,50} = 25, and m can be any of 50 values.
$p = 50 \times 25 = 1250$
For $m + n$ = square of prime, possible values are 4, 9, 25, 49.
$m + n = 4$: 3 pairs
$m + n = 9$: 8 pairs
$m + n = 25$: 24 pairs
$m + n = 49$: 48 pairs
$q = 3 + 8 + 24 + 48 = 83$
$p + q = 1250 + 83 = 1333$

38937.subject: Physics
38937.text:
In the hydrogen atom, the electron makes a transition from the higher orbit ($i$) to a lower orbit ($f$). The ratio of the radius of the orbits in given by $r_i : r_f = 16 : 4$. The wavelength of photon emitted due to this transition is _____ nm.
(Given Rydberg constant $= 1.0973 \times 10^7$ /m)
38937.sol:
The radius of the $n$-th orbit in a hydrogen atom is proportional to the square of the principal quantum number $n$, i.e., $r_n \propto n^2$.

Given the ratio of the radii of the initial and final orbits:
$\dfrac{r_i}{r_f} = \dfrac{16}{4}$

This implies:
$\dfrac{n_i^2}{n_f^2} = \dfrac{16}{4} \Rightarrow n_i = 4 \text{ and } n_f = 2$

The wavelength $\lambda$ of the emitted photon is given by the Rydberg formula:
$\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = R \left( \dfrac{1}{n_f^2} - \dfrac{1}{n_i^2} \right)$

Substituting the values:
$\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = 1.0973 \times 10^7 \left( \dfrac{1}{2^2} - \dfrac{1}{4^2} \right)$

$\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = 1.0973 \times 10^7 \left( \dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{16} \right)$

$\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = 1.0973 \times 10^7 \times \dfrac{3}{16}$

$\lambda = \dfrac{16}{3 \times 1.0973 \times 10^7} \text{ m}$

$\lambda \approx 4.86 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m} = 486 \text{ nm}$

Answer: $486$

39190.text:
A parallel plate capacitor with plate area '$A$' and distance of separation '$d$' is filled with a dielectric. What is the capacity of the capacitor when permittivity of the dielectric varies as:

$ε\left(x\right) = {ε}_{0} + kx$, for $\left(0 < x \le \dfrac{d}{2}\right)$

$ε\left(x\right) = {ε}_{0} + k\left(d - x\right)$, for $\left(\dfrac{d}{2} \le x \le d\right)$
39190.sol:
Taking an element of width dx at a distance $x\left(x < d / 2\right)$ from left plate

$dc = \dfrac{( {ε}_{0} + kx )A}{dx}$

Capacitance of half of the capacitor

$\dfrac{1}{C} = {∫}_{0}^{d / 2}\dfrac{1}{dc} = \dfrac{1}{A}{∫}_{0}^{d / 2}\dfrac{dx}{{ε}_{0} + kx}$

$\dfrac{1}{C} = \dfrac{1}{kA}ln\left(\dfrac{{ε}_{0} + kd / 2}{{ε}_{0}}\right)$

Capacitance of second half will be same

${C}_{eq} = \dfrac{C}{2} = \dfrac{kA}{2ln\left(\dfrac{2{ε}_{0} + kd}{2{ε}_{0}}\right)}$

39515.subject: Physics
39515.text: The voltage and the current between $A$ and $B$ points shown in the circuit are _____.
39515.sol:
The four parallel branches between the common left node $A$ and the common right node are all identical: each consists of a $27\text{ V}$ source in series with a $3\ \Omega$ resistor. In the third branch, the two cells $(14\text{ V}$ and $13\text{ V})$ aid each other, giving a net EMF of $14 + 13 = 27\text{ V}$.

Thevenin equivalent between $A$ and $B$:
Since all four branches have the same EMF and polarity in parallel:
$V_{th} = 27\text{ V}$

The four $3\ \Omega$ resistors in parallel give:
$R_{th} = \dfrac{3}{4} = 0.75\ \Omega$

Load branch (diagonal):
The diagonal connecting $A$ and $B$ consists of two $3\ \Omega$ resistors in series, so:
$R_L = 3 + 3 = 6\ \Omega$

Current through the diagonal branch:
$I = \dfrac{V_{th}}{R_{th} + R_L} = \dfrac{27}{0.75 + 6} = \dfrac{27}{6.75} = 4\text{ A}$

Voltage across $A$ and $B$:
$V_{AB} = I \cdot R_L = 4 \times 6 = 24\text{ V}$

Hence, the voltage is $24\text{ V}$ and the current is $4\text{ A}$, which corresponds to option $(2)\ 24\text{ V},\ 4\text{ A}$.

39657.text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : A uniform wire of resistance $80Ω$ is cut into four equal parts. These parts are now connected in parallel. The equivalent resistance of the combination will be $5Ω$.

Statement II : Two resistance $2R$ and $3R$ are connected in parallel in an electric circuit. The value of thermal energy developed in $3R$ and $2R$ will be in the ratio $3: 2$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct.
39657.sol:
Statement $1 -$ $R = 80Ω$

When it is cut into $4$ equal parts, the resistance of each part will be,

${R}_{1} = {R}_{2} = {R}_{3} = {R}_{4} = 20Ω$

When these resistances are connected in parallel,

${R}_{eq} = \dfrac{20}{4} = 5Ω$

Hence, the statement I is correct.

Statement 2 -

When the resistances are connected in parallel, the potential difference between them is same. Therefore, the power consumed can be written as,

$P = \dfrac{{V}^{2}}{R}$

$⇒ \dfrac{{P}_{1}}{{P}_{2}} = \left(\dfrac{{R}_{2}}{{R}_{1}}\right) = \dfrac{2}{3}$

Hence, statement II is incorrect.

47858.subject: Chemistry
47858.text:
Statement I: Staggered conformation of ethane is more stable than the eclipsed conformation.
Statement II: The torsional strain in staggered conformation is more.
Read the above statements and choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
47858.sol:
Statement I is true because in the staggered conformation of ethane, the electron clouds of the C-H bonds on adjacent carbon atoms are as far apart as possible. This minimizes the repulsive forces between them, making the staggered conformation more stable than the eclipsed conformation.

Statement II is false because torsional strain arises from the repulsive interaction between the electron clouds of adjacent bonds. In the staggered conformation, this repulsion is at a minimum, so the torsional strain is minimum, not more. It is maximum in the eclipsed conformation.

Therefore, Statement I is true but Statement II is false.

Answer: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

The reduction half-reaction is:
$\text{MnO}_4^- + 8\text{H}^+ + 5e^- \rightarrow \text{Mn}^{2+} + 4\text{H}_2\text{O}$

To balance the number of electrons, multiply the oxidation half-reaction by $5$ and the reduction half-reaction by $2$:
$5\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} \rightarrow 10\text{CO}_2 + 10e^-$
$2\text{MnO}_4^- + 16\text{H}^+ + 10e^- \rightarrow 2\text{Mn}^{2+} + 8\text{H}_2\text{O}$

Adding the two balanced half-reactions, we get:
$5\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} + 2\text{MnO}_4^- + 16\text{H}^+ \rightarrow 2\text{Mn}^{2+} + 8\text{H}_2\text{O} + 10\text{CO}_2$

Comparing this with the given equation $a\text{C}_2\text{O}_4^{2-} + b\text{MnO}_4^- + c\text{H}^+ \rightarrow x\text{Mn}^{2+} + y\text{H}_2\text{O} + z\text{CO}_2$, we find:
$a = 5$
$b = 2$
$c = 16$
$x = 2$
$y = 8$
$z = 10$

Thus, the values of $a$ and $x$ are $5$ and $2$ respectively.

Answer: $5, 2$

48819.subject: Mathematics
48819.text: If A and B are invertible square matrices of order n, then which of the following is not correct?
48819.sol:
For any two square matrices $A$ and $B$ of the same order, the determinant of their product is the product of their determinants, so $\det(AB) = \det(A) \cdot \det(B)$.

If $A$ is a square matrix of order $n$ and $k$ is a scalar, then multiplying $A$ by $k$ multiplies each of its $n$ rows by $k$. Thus, $\det(kA) = k^n \det(A)$.

For an invertible matrix $A$, $A A^{-1} = I$. Taking the determinant on both sides gives $\det(A) \cdot \det(A^{-1}) = \det(I) = 1$, which implies $\det(A^{-1}) = \dfrac{1}{\det(A)}$.

However, the determinant of a sum of matrices is generally not equal to the sum of their determinants. Therefore, $\det(A + B) = \det(A) + \det(B)$ is not correct.

Answer: $\det(A + B) = \det(A) + \det(B)$

$\therefore \quad\left(r_0\right)_{\alpha_f}=\frac{\left(r_0\right) \alpha_i}{4}=\frac{d}{4} \quad\left[\because\left(r_0\right)_{\alpha_i}=d\right]$

54918.text: Which of the following is primary allylic alcohol?
54918.sol:
A primary allylic alcohol requires that the hydroxyl group is attached to a carbon adjacent to a carbon-carbon double bond (allylic) and that the hydroxyl-bearing carbon is only attached to one other carbon (primary).

Option A: $\mathrm{H_2 C=CH-CH(CH_3)-OH}$ is allylic and secondary.

Option C: $\mathrm{H_2 C=CH-C(CH_3)_2 -OH}$ is allylic and tertiary.

Option D: $\mathrm{CH_3 -CH=CH-CH(CH_3)-OH}$ is allylic and secondary.

Option B: $\mathrm{H_2 C=CH-CH_2 -OH}$ is allylic since the $\mathrm{CH_2}$ group is adjacent to the double bond, and primary as the hydroxyl-bearing carbon attaches to only one other carbon.

The correct primary allylic alcohol is $\boxed{B}$.

58419.subject: Chemistry
58419.text: Which from following polymers does NOT contain either —COO— or —CO—NH— linkage in it?
58419.sol:
To identify which polymer lacks both ester (—COO—) and amide (—CO—NH—) linkages, examine the structural composition of each:

Perspex (polymethyl methacrylate) contains ester linkages from its methyl methacrylate monomer $\mathrm{CH_2=C(CH_3)COOCH_3}$, forming $[—\mathrm{CH_2—C(CH_3)(COOCH_3)—}]_n$.

Polyacrylamide includes amide linkages derived from acrylamide $\mathrm{CH_2=CHCONH_2}$, yielding $[—\mathrm{CH_2—CH(CONH_2)—}]_n$.

Glyptal, a polyester resin synthesized from phthalic acid and glycerol, inherently contains ester linkages.

Thermocol (polystyrene) polymerizes from styrene $\mathrm{C_6 H_5CH=CH_2}$ via addition polymerization, resulting in $[—\mathrm{CH(C_6 H_5)—CH_2—}]_n$ with a hydrocarbon backbone and phenyl substituents, devoid of ester or amide functional groups.

Thus, Thermocol is the polymer without —COO— or —CO—NH— linkages.

58814.subject: Chemistry
58814.text: When silver crystallizes, it forms face centered cubic cells, if the volume of unit cells $6.84 \times 10^{-23}\ \text{cm}^3$. Calculate the density of silver. (Molar mass of silver is 108 g/mol, $N_A = 6.022 \times 10^{23}$)
58814.sol:
For a face-centered cubic (fcc) unit cell, the number of atoms per unit cell is $Z = 4$.

The density of the unit cell is given by the formula:

$d = \dfrac{Z \times M}{N_A \times V}$

Substituting the given values:

$d = \dfrac{4 \times 108}{6.022 \times 10^{23} \times 6.84 \times 10^{-23}}$

$d = \dfrac{432}{41.19}$

$d = 10.49\ \text{gm cm}^{-3}$

Answer: $10.49\ \text{gm cm}^{-3}$

59929.subject: Chemistry
59929.text: Identify from following reactions that exhibits negative work done.
59929.sol:
Negative work occurs when the system expands at constant pressure, which requires a positive change in gaseous moles. The work done is given by $W = -\Delta n_g RT$, where $\Delta n_g$ is the change in the number of moles of gaseous species.

For reaction A: $2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_{2(\ell)} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}_{(\ell)} + \mathrm{O}_{2(\mathrm{g})}$
Gaseous products: 1, reactants: 0, so $\Delta n_g = 1 > 0$. Hence, $W < 0$.

For reaction B: $\mathrm{NH}_{3(\mathrm{g})} + \mathrm{HCl}_{(\mathrm{g})} \rightarrow \mathrm{NH}_4\mathrm{Cl}_{(\mathrm{s})}$
Gaseous products: 0, reactants: 2, so $\Delta n_g = -2 < 0$. Hence, $W > 0$.

For reaction C: $\mathrm{H}_{2(\mathrm{g})} + \mathrm{Cl}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{HCl}_{(\mathrm{g})}$
Gaseous products: 2, reactants: 2, so $\Delta n_g = 0$. Hence, $W = 0$.

For reaction D: $\mathrm{N}_{2(\mathrm{g})} + 3\mathrm{H}_{2(\mathrm{g})} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NH}_{3(\mathrm{g})}$
Gaseous products: 2, reactants: 4, so $\Delta n_g = -2 < 0$. Hence, $W > 0$.

Only reaction A exhibits negative work done.

60210.subject: Mathematics
60210.text: The function $f(x) = \tan^{-1}(\sin x + \cos x)$ is an increasing function in the interval.....
60210.sol:
Given $f(x) = \tan^{-1}(\sin x + \cos x)$

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get:

$f'(x) = \dfrac{1}{1 + (\sin x + \cos x)^2} \times \dfrac{d}{dx}(\sin x + \cos x)$

$f'(x) = \dfrac{\cos x - \sin x}{1 + (\sin x + \cos x)^2}$

For $f(x)$ to be an increasing function, $f'(x) \gt 0$.

Since the denominator $1 + (\sin x + \cos x)^2$ is always positive for all real $x$, the sign of $f'(x)$ depends entirely on the numerator.

$\Rightarrow \cos x - \sin x \gt 0$

$\Rightarrow \cos x \gt \sin x$

From the standard trigonometric graphs, the inequality $\cos x \gt \sin x$ holds true in the interval $\left(\dfrac{-\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$.

Therefore, the function is increasing in the interval $\left(\dfrac{-\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$.

Answer: $\left(\dfrac{-\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$

60266.subject: Mathematics
60266.text: If $x$ is real, then the difference between the greatest and least values of $\frac{x^2-x+1}{x^2+x+1}$ is
60266.sol:
Let $y = \frac{x^2 - x + 1}{x^2 + x + 1}$. To determine the range of $y$, we eliminate the denominator and rearrange:

$y(x^2 + x + 1) = x^2 - x + 1$
$yx^2 + yx + y = x^2 - x + 1$
$(y - 1)x^2 + (y + 1)x + (y - 1) = 0$

For real $x$, the discriminant $D$ of this quadratic must satisfy $D \geq 0$:

$D = (y + 1)^2 - 4(y - 1)^2 \geq 0$
$(y + 1)^2 - 4(y - 1)^2 \geq 0$
$(3 - y)(3y - 1) \geq 0$

This inequality holds for $\frac{1}{3} \leq y \leq 3$, including $y = 1$ as $x = 0$ is valid.

The range is $[\frac{1}{3}, 3]$, so the greatest value is $3$ and the least is $\frac{1}{3}$. The difference is:

$3 - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{8}{3}$

60911.text: The value of f(0) so that the function $f(x) = \dfrac{(256 - 8x)^{\frac{1}{4}} - 4}{16 - 4(64 + 3x)^{\frac{1}{3}}}$, $x \neq 0$ is continuous at $x = 0$, is
60911.sol:
For $f(x)$ to be continuous at $x = 0$, we must have $f(0) = \lim_{x \to 0} f(x)$.

$\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{(256 - 8x)^{\dfrac{1}{4}} - 4}{16 - 4(64 + 3x)^{\dfrac{1}{3}}}$

This is a $\dfrac{0}{0}$ indeterminate form. Applying L'Hospital's rule:

$\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{4}(256 - 8x)^{-\dfrac{3}{4}} \times (-8)}{-4 \times \dfrac{1}{3}(64 + 3x)^{-\dfrac{2}{3}} \times 3}$

$= \lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{-2(256 - 8x)^{-\dfrac{3}{4}}}{-4(64 + 3x)^{-\dfrac{2}{3}}}$

Substituting $x = 0$:

$= \dfrac{-2(256)^{-\dfrac{3}{4}}}{-4(64)^{-\dfrac{2}{3}}}$

$= \dfrac{-2(4^4)^{-\dfrac{3}{4}}}{-4(4^3)^{-\dfrac{2}{3}}}$

$= \dfrac{-2(4^{-3})}{-4(4^{-2})}$

$= \dfrac{-2 \times \dfrac{1}{64}}{-4 \times \dfrac{1}{16}}$

$= \dfrac{-\dfrac{1}{32}}{-\dfrac{1}{4}} = \dfrac{1}{8}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{8}$

61319.text: The differential equation which represents the family of curves $\mathrm{y}=\mathrm{C}_1 \mathrme^{\mathrm{c}_2 x}$, where $\mathrm{C}_1, \mathrm{C}_2$ are arbitrary constants is
61319.sol:
The family of curves $y = C_1 e^{c_2 x}$ contains two arbitrary constants $C_1$ and $C_2$, requiring a second-order differential equation to eliminate them.

Differentiating $y = C_1 e^{c_2 x}$ gives $y' = C_1 c_2 e^{c_2 x}$, and differentiating again yields $y'' = C_1 c_2^2 e^{c_2 x}$.

From the first derivative, $y' = c_2 y$ since $C_1 e^{c_2 x} = y$, giving $c_2 = \frac{y'}{y}$.

Similarly, $y'' = c_2 y'$ by substituting $C_1 c_2 e^{c_2 x} = y'$ into the second derivative.

Substituting $c_2 = \frac{y'}{y}$ into $y'' = c_2 y'$ produces $y'' = \frac{(y')^2}{y}$, which rearranges to the differential equation $yy'' = (y')^2$.

This matches option C: $yy'' = (y')^2$.

options: $\tan ^{-1}(x+y)=x+c, \quad$ where $c$ is the constant of integration
$x+\mathrm{y}=\tan x+\mathrm{c}, \quad$ where c is the constant of integration

$x+\mathrm{y}=\sin ^{-1}(x+\mathrm{y})+\mathrm{c}$, where c is the constant of integration
61359.sol:
Solve the differential equation $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = (x + y)^2$ by substituting $z = x + y$.

Differentiating the substitution with respect to $x$ gives $\frac{\mathrm{d}z}{\mathrm{d}x} = 1 + \frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x}$, so $\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}x} = \frac{\mathrm{d}z}{\mathrm{d}x} - 1$.

Substituting into the original equation yields $\frac{\mathrm{d}z}{\mathrm{d}x} - 1 = z^2$, which rearranges to $\frac{\mathrm{d}z}{\mathrm{d}x} = 1 + z^2$.

Separate variables: $\frac{\mathrm{d}z}{1 + z^2} = \mathrm{d}x$, then integrate both sides: $\int \frac{\mathrm{d}z}{1 + z^2} = \int \mathrm{d}x$.

The left side is $\tan^{-1}(z)$, and the right side is $x + c$, where $c$ is the integration constant.

Thus, $\tan^{-1}(z) = x + c$, and substituting back $z = x + y$ gives $\tan^{-1}(x + y) = x + c$.

The solution corresponds to option A, so the final answer is $\boxed{\text{A}}$.

61508.sol:

& \therefore x \frac{d v}{d x}=-\frac{3 v+v^2}{1+v}- v=-\frac{\left(2 v^2+4 v\right)}{1+v}
\end{aligned} \begin{aligned}& \therefore \int \frac{1+v}{\left(2 v^2+4 v\right)} d v=\int \frac{-1}{x} d x \\
& \therefore \frac{1}{2} \int \frac{v+1}{v^2+2 v} d v=-\int \frac{d x}{x} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{4} \int \frac{2(v+1)}{v^2+2 v} d v=-\log x+\log c_1
\end{aligned} \begin{aligned}& \therefore \frac{1}{4} \log \left(\mathrm{v}^2+2 \mathrm{v}\right)+\log \mathrm{x}=\log \mathrm{c}_{1} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{4} \log \left(\frac{\mathrm{y}^2}{\mathrm{x}^2}+\frac{2 \mathrm{y}}{\mathrm{x}}\right)+\log \mathrm{x}=\log \mathrm{c}_{1} \\
& \therefore \frac{1}{4} \log \left(\frac{\mathrm{y}^2+2 \mathrm{xy}}{\mathrm{x}^2}\right)+\log \mathrm{x}=\log \mathrm{c}_{1} \Rightarrow \log \left(\frac{\mathrm{y}^2+2 \mathrm{xy}}{\mathrm{x}^2}\right)+\log \mathrm{x}^4=4 \log \mathrm{c}_{1} \\
& \therefore \log\left[\left(\frac{\mathrm{y}^2+2 \mathrm{xy}}{\mathrm{x}^2}\right)\left(\mathrm{x}^4\right)\right]=\log \mathrm{c}_{1}^4 \Rightarrow \log \left[\mathrm{x}^2\left(\mathrm{y}^2+2 \mathrm{xy}\right)\right]=\log \mathrm{c}_{1}^4 \\
& \therefore \mathrm{x}^2\left(\mathrm{y}^2+2 \mathrm{xy}\right)=\mathrm{c} \end{aligned}$

63562.subject: Mathematics
63562.text: If in $6$ trials, X is a binomial random variable which follows the relation $9P(x = 4) = P(x = 2)$, then the probability of failure is...
63562.sol:
Let $p$ be the probability of success and $q$ be the probability of failure in a single trial, where $p + q = 1$.

For a binomial distribution with $n = 6$ trials, the probability of $x$ successes is given by $P(X = x) = ^{6}C_{x} p^{x} q^{6-x}$.

Given the relation:

$9P(X = 4) = P(X = 2)$

Substituting the binomial probabilities:

$9 \times ^{6}C_{4} p^{4} q^{2} = ^{6}C_{2} p^{2} q^{4}$

Since ^{6}C_{4} = ^{6}C_{2} = 15$, we can cancel it from both sides:

9 p^{4} q^{2} = p^{2} q^{4}$

Dividing both sides by $p^{2} q^{2}$ (assuming $p, q \neq 0$):

$9 p^{2} = q^{2}$

Taking the square root on both sides (since probabilities are non-negative):

$3p = q$

We know that $p + q = 1$. Substituting $p = \dfrac{q}{3}$:

$\dfrac{q}{3} + q = 1$

$\dfrac{4q}{3} = 1$

$q = \dfrac{3}{4} = 0.75$

Thus, the probability of failure is $0.75$.

63615.subject: Mathematics
63615.text: The probability that a person is not a sportsperson is $\frac{1}{6}. Then the probability that out of the 6 members of the family, 5 are sportspersons is$
63615.sol:
The probability that a person is not a sportsperson is given as $P(\text{not } S) = \frac{1}{6}$. The complement yields the probability of being a sportsperson: $P(S) = 1 - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{5}{6}$.

Finding the probability that exactly 5 out of 6 family members are sportspersons is a binomial probability problem. Using the binomial formula $P(X = k) = C(n, k) p^k q^{n-k}$ with $n = 6$, $k = 5$, $p = \frac{5}{6}$, and $q = \frac{1}{6}$, we compute:

$P(X = 5) = C(6,5) \left(\frac{5}{6}\right)^5 \left(\frac{1}{6}\right)^1$

Since $C(6,5) = 6$, this simplifies to:

$P(X = 5) = 6 \cdot \frac{5^5}{6^5} \cdot \frac{1}{6} = \frac{5^5}{6^5} = \left(\frac{5}{6}\right)^5$

This matches option A.

64382.subject: Mathematics
64382.text: The lines $\dfrac{x - 2}{1} = \dfrac{y - 3}{1} = \dfrac{z - 4}{-k}$ and $\dfrac{x - 1}{k} = \dfrac{y - 4}{2} = \dfrac{z - 5}{1}$ are coplanar if
64382.sol:
The condition for two lines $\dfrac{x - x_1}{a_1} = \dfrac{y - y_1}{b_1} = \dfrac{z - z_1}{c_1}$ and $\dfrac{x - x_2}{a_2} = \dfrac{y - y_2}{b_2} = \dfrac{z - z_2}{c_2}$ to be coplanar is:

$\begin{vmatrix} x_2 - x_1 \text{ and } y_2 - y_1 \text{ and } z_2 - z_1 \\ a_1 \text{ and } b_1 \text{ and } c_1 \\ a_2 \text{ and } b_2 \text{ and } c_2 \end{vmatrix} = 0$

From the given equations of the lines, we have $(x_1, y_1, z_1) = (2, 3, 4)$ and $(x_2, y_2, z_2) = (1, 4, 5)$.

The direction ratios are $(a_1, b_1, c_1) = (1, 1, -k)$ and $(a_2, b_2, c_2) = (k, 2, 1)$.

Substituting these values into the determinant condition:

$\begin{vmatrix} 1 - 2 \text{ and } 4 - 3 \text{ and } 5 - 4 \\ 1 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } -k \\ k \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } 1 \end{vmatrix} = 0$

$\begin{vmatrix} -1 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } 1 \\ 1 \text{ and } 1 \text{ and } -k \\ k \text{ and } 2 \text{ and } 1 \end{vmatrix} = 0$

Expanding the determinant along the first row:

$-1(1 \cdot 1 - (-k) \cdot 2) - 1(1 \cdot 1 - (-k) \cdot k) + 1(1 \cdot 2 - 1 \cdot k) = 0$

$-1(1 + 2k) - 1(1 + k^2) + 1(2 - k) = 0$

$-1 - 2k - 1 - k^2 + 2 - k = 0$

$-k^2 - 3k = 0$

$k(k + 3) = 0$

$\Rightarrow k = 0, -3$

Answer: $k = 0, -3$

64477.text: The co-ordinates of the point where the line joining the points $(2,-3,1)$ and $(3,-4,-5)$ and intersects the plane $2 x+y+z=7$ are
64477.sol:
Given points $P_1(2,-3,1)$ and $P_2(3,-4,-5)$, the direction vector of the line is $\vec{d} = (1,-1,-6)$.

The parametric equations of the line through $P_1$ are:
$x = 2 + t$
$y = -3 - t$
$z = 1 - 6t$

Substituting into the plane equation $2x + y + z = 7$ gives:
$2(2+t) + (-3-t) + (1-6t) = 7$

Simplifying:
$4 + 2t - 3 - t + 1 - 6t = 7$
$2 - 5t = 7$
$t = -1$

Substituting $t = -1$ back into the parametric equations yields the intersection point $(1, -2, 7)$, which corresponds to option D.

The correct answer is $\boxed{\text{D}}$.

65064.subject: Mathematics
65064.text: If $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$ are unit vectors perpendicular to each other, then $\left[\bar{a} + (\bar{a} \times \bar{b})\quad \bar{b} + (\bar{a} \times \bar{b})\quad (\bar{a} \times \bar{b})\right] = \cdots$
65064.sol:
Let $\bar{c} = \bar{a} \times \bar{b}$.

The given scalar triple product is $[\bar{a} + \bar{c} \quad \bar{b} + \bar{c} \quad \bar{c}]$.

Using the properties of the scalar triple product:

$[\bar{a} + \bar{c} \quad \bar{b} + \bar{c} \quad \bar{c}] = (\bar{a} + \bar{c}) \cdot ((\bar{b} + \bar{c}) \times \bar{c})$

$= (\bar{a} + \bar{c}) \cdot (\bar{b} \times \bar{c} + \bar{c} \times \bar{c})$

Since $\bar{c} \times \bar{c} = \bar{0}$, we get:

$= (\bar{a} + \bar{c}) \cdot (\bar{b} \times \bar{c})$

$= \bar{a} \cdot (\bar{b} \times \bar{c}) + \bar{c} \cdot (\bar{b} \times \bar{c})$

Since the scalar triple product with two identical vectors is zero, $\bar{c} \cdot (\bar{b} \times \bar{c}) = 0$.

$= \bar{a} \cdot (\bar{b} \times \bar{c}) = [\bar{a} \quad \bar{b} \quad \bar{c}]$

Substituting $\bar{c} = \bar{a} \times \bar{b}$ back into the expression:

$[\bar{a} \quad \bar{b} \quad \bar{a} \times \bar{b}] = (\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) \cdot (\bar{a} \times \bar{b}) = |\bar{a} \times \bar{b}|^2$

Since $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$ are unit vectors perpendicular to each other, $|\bar{a}| = 1$, $|\bar{b}| = 1$, and the angle between them is $90^{{}^{\circ}}$.

$|\bar{a} \times \bar{b}| = |\bar{a}| |\bar{b}| \sin 90^{{}^{\circ}} = 1 \times 1 \times 1 = 1$

Therefore, $|\bar{a} \times \bar{b}|^2 = 1$.

65578.text: In series LCR circuit, resistance is $18\ \Omega$ and impedance $33\ \Omega$. An r.m.s. Voltage of $220$ V is applied across the circuit. The true power consumed in a c. circuit is
65578.sol:
The true power consumed in an AC circuit is given by the formula:

$P = I_{rms}^2 R$

The rms current in the circuit is:

$I_{rms} = \dfrac{V_{rms}}{Z}$

Substituting the given values $V_{rms} = 220$ V and $Z = 33\ \Omega$:

$I_{rms} = \dfrac{220}{33} = \dfrac{20}{3}$ A

Now, substituting $I_{rms}$ and $R = 18\ \Omega$ into the power formula:

$P = \left(\dfrac{20}{3}\right)^2 \times 18$

$P = \dfrac{400}{9} \times 18$

$P = 800$ W

Answer: $800$ W

$U = \dfrac{1}{2}LI^2$

Substituting the given values, $L = 4$ H and $I = 1.5$ A:

$U = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 4 \times (1.5)^2$

Answer: $4500$ mJ

67216.subject: Physics
67216.text: A body is projected vertically from earth's surface of radius R with velocity equal to half the escape velocity. The maximum height reached by the body is
67216.sol:
Escape velocity from the surface of the earth is given by $v_e = \sqrt{\dfrac{2GM}{R}}$

Initial velocity of the body is $v = \dfrac{v_e}{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{2R}}$

Applying conservation of mechanical energy at the surface of the earth and at maximum height $h$:

$K_i + U_i = K_f + U_f$

$\dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 - \dfrac{GMm}{R} = 0 - \dfrac{GMm}{R+h}$

Substituting the value of $v^2$:

$\dfrac{1}{2}m\left(\dfrac{GM}{2R}\right) - \dfrac{GMm}{R} = - \dfrac{GMm}{R+h}$

$\dfrac{GMm}{4R} - \dfrac{GMm}{R} = - \dfrac{GMm}{R+h}$

$-\dfrac{3GMm}{4R} = - \dfrac{GMm}{R+h}$

$\dfrac{3}{4R} = \dfrac{1}{R+h}$

$3R + 3h = 4R$

$3h = R \Rightarrow h = \dfrac{R}{3}$

Answer: $\dfrac{R}{3}$

70142.text: For obtaining maximum contrast between the bright and dark fringes in an interference pattern, the intensities of the two light coherent sources should be
70142.sol:
The contrast of an interference pattern is determined by the visibility, which is given by $V = \dfrac{I_\max - I_\min}{I_\max + I_\min}$.

For maximum contrast, the minimum intensity $I_\min$ should be zero.

The minimum intensity in an interference pattern is given by $I_\min = (\sqrt{I_1} - \sqrt{I_2})^2$.

For $I_\min = 0$, we must have $\sqrt{I_1} = \sqrt{I_2}, which implies $I_1 = I_2$.

Thus, the intensities of the two coherent sources should be equal.

Answer: equal$

71008.subject: Biology
71008.text: Which one of the following respiratory disorders is NOT caused by bacteria or viruses?
71008.sol:
Chronic bronchitis is a long-term inflammation of the bronchi, primarily caused by prolonged exposure to respiratory irritants such as cigarette smoke, air pollution, or occupational dust and chemicals. It is a major component of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) and is not caused by bacterial or viral infections.

In contrast, acute bronchitis, laryngitis, and sinusitis are frequently caused by viral or bacterial infections.

Answer: Chronic bronchitis

71292.subject: Biology
71292.sol:
The unequivocal proof that DNA is the genetic material came from the experiments of Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase in 1952.

They worked with viruses that infect bacteria, which are called bacteriophages (specifically the T2 bacteriophage).

In their experiment, they used radioactive isotopes of phosphorus (^{32}$\text{P} ) and sulfur (^{35}\text{S}$) to label the DNA and protein coat of the bacteriophages, respectively, to determine which of these molecules enters the bacterial cell (Escherichia coli) during infection.

Answer: Bacteriophages

72076.text: The potential differences across the resistor, capacitor and inductor are $80$ V, $40$ and $100$ V respectively in series LCR circuit. The power factor of this circuit is
72076.sol:
Given $V_R = 80$ V, $V_C = 40$ V, and $V_L = 100$ V.

The total voltage $V$ across the series LCR circuit is given by:

$V = \sqrt{V_R^2 + (V_L - V_C)^2}$

Substituting the given values:

$V = \sqrt{80^2 + (100 - 40)^2}$

$V = \sqrt{80^2 + 60^2}$

$V = \sqrt{6400 + 3600} = \sqrt{10000} = 100$ V

The power factor of the circuit is:

$\cos \phi = \dfrac{V_R}{V}$

$\cos \phi = \dfrac{80}{100} = 0.8$

Answer: $0.8$

72095.text: In a series LCR circuit, the inductance L is 10 mH, capacitance C is 100$\mu$ F and resistance R is 20 $\Omega$. The frequency at which impedance is 20 $\Omega$, is
72095.sol:
Given $L = 10 \text{ mH} = 10^{-2} \text{ H}$, $C = 100 \mu\text{F} = 10^{-4} \text{ F}$, and $R = 20 \Omega$.

The impedance of a series LCR circuit is given by $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + \left(X_L - X_C\right)^2}$.

Since $Z = 20 \Omega = R$, the circuit is in resonance, which implies $X_L = X_C$.

$\omega L = \dfrac{1}{\omega C} \Rightarrow \omega = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$

Substituting the values of $L$ and $C$:

$\omega = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{10^{-2} \times 10^{-4}}} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{10^{-6}}} = 10^3 \text{ rad/s}$

The frequency $f$ is given by $f = \dfrac{\omega}{2\pi}$.

$f = \dfrac{10^3}{2\pi} \text{ Hz}$

Answer: $\dfrac{10^3}{2\pi}$

72386.text:
A p-n junction photodiode is fabricated from a semiconductor with a band gap of $4 \times 10^{-19}$ J. It can detect a signal of wavelength
$[h = 6.6 \times 10^{-34} \text{Js} , C = 3 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}]$
72386.sol:
For a photodiode to detect a signal, the energy of the incident photon must be greater than or equal to the band gap energy of the semiconductor.

$E \ge E_g$

$\dfrac{hc}{\lambda} \ge E_g$

$\lambda \le \dfrac{hc}{E_g}$

Substituting the given values:

$\lambda \le \dfrac{6.6 \times 10^{-34} \times 3 \times 10^8}{4 \times 10^{-19}}$

$\lambda \le \dfrac{19.8 \times 10^{-26}}{4 \times 10^{-19}}$

$\lambda \le 4.95 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$

$\lambda \le 4950 \text{ \AA}$

Among the given options, only $4000 \text{ \AA}$ is less than $4950 \text{ \AA}$.

Answer: $4000$ Å

72605.text:
The following items have a blank space followed by four options. Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank and mark your response on the Answer Sheet accordingly.

I __________ consider the opinions of all stakeholders before taking a final decision.
72605.sol:
The blank requires a modal auxiliary verb to express a future action or formal intention.

The verb consider is in its base form. Therefore, the auxiliary verb have is incorrect, as it must be followed by the past participle considered.

The phrase will not provides a negative meaning that contradicts the constructive and cooperative nature of taking a final decision.

According to traditional English grammar, the modal verb shall is specifically used with first-person pronouns such as I and we to express formal intention, determination, or future action.

Therefore, shall is the most grammatically appropriate and formal choice to complete the sentence.

Answer: shall

73842.subject: General Ability
73842.text: An object is placed between infinity and the pole (P) of a convex mirror. The position of the image is
options: between pole (P) and the focus (F), behind the mirror
between the focus (F) and infinity, behind the mirror
between the pole (P) and the infinity, in front of the mirror
at the focus (F), behind the mirror
73842.sol:
Using the mirror formula:

$\dfrac{1}{v} + \dfrac{1}{u} = \dfrac{1}{f}$

$\dfrac{1}{v} = \dfrac{1}{f} - \dfrac{1}{u}$

For a convex mirror, the focal length $f$ is positive ($f > 0$). The object is placed in front of the mirror, so the object distance $u$ is negative ($u < 0$).

Since $f > 0$ and $u < 0$, the term $-\dfrac{1}{u}$ is positive. Therefore, $\dfrac{1}{v}$ is the sum of two positive quantities, which means $\dfrac{1}{v} > \dfrac{1}{f}$.

This implies that $v < f$. Also, since $\dfrac{1}{v} > 0$, we have $v > 0$.

Thus, $0 < v < f$. The image is formed between the pole (P) and the focus (F), behind the mirror.

Answer: between pole (P) and the focus (F), behind the mirror

75192.text:
Which of the following rights under the Constitution of India is/are Fundamental Right(s)?
1. Right to work
2. Right to privacy
3. Right to free and compulsory education in the age bracket of six to eighteen years
Select the answer using the code given below:
75192.sol:
Statement 1 is incorrect. The Right to work is a Directive Principle of State Policy under Article 41 of the Constitution of India, not a Fundamental Right.

Statement 2 is correct. The Right to privacy is recognized as a Fundamental Right under Article 21 (Right to Life and Personal Liberty) following the Supreme Court's landmark judgment in the K.S. Puttaswamy case.

Statement 3 is incorrect. The Right to Education under Article 21A provides for free and compulsory education to all children in the age group of six to fourteen years, not six to eighteen years.

Therefore, only statement 2 represents a Fundamental Right.

Answer: 2 only

76667.text: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the distinct roots of equation $x^2-x+1=0$, then what is the value of $\left|\frac{\alpha^{100}+\beta^{100}}{\alpha^{100}-\beta^{100}}\right|$ ?
76667.sol:
$x^2-x+1=0$
We know that roots of $x^2+x+1=0$ are $\omega$ and $\omega^2$.
$\therefore \quad$ Roots of $x^2-x+1=0$ are $-\omega$ and $-\omega^2$
where $\omega, \omega^2$ are complex cube roots of unity
$\therefore\left|\frac{\alpha^{100}+\beta^{100}}{\alpha^{100}-\beta^{100}}\right|=\left|\frac{\omega^{100}+\left(\omega^2\right)^{100}}{\omega^{100}-\left(\omega^2\right)^{100}}\right|=\left|\frac{\omega+\omega^2}{\omega-\omega^2}\right|=\left|\frac{-1}{\omega-\omega^2}\right|=\left|\frac{-1}{\frac{-1+\sqrt{3} i}{2}-\frac{(-1-\sqrt{3} i)}{2}}\right|=\left|\frac{-1}{\sqrt{3} i}\right|=\left|\frac{i}{\sqrt{3}}\right|=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

79594.text: In which group of organisms the cell walls form two thin lapping shells which fit together?
79594.sol: CHRYSOPHYTES: Chrysophytes include diatoms and golden algae (desmids). These are found both in fresh and marine water. They are microscopic and float passively (without using energy) in water currents. Most of Chrysophytes are photosynthetic. Silica is deposited in the cell wall of diatoms. The cell walls form two thin overlapping shells, which fit together as in a soapbox. During asexual reproduction, each daughter cell retains one half of the old wall and synthesizes a new half. Diatoms are normally diploid and reproduce sexually by producing gametes. Silica shells of dead diatoms are nearly indestructible and thus, get accumulated at their habitat. Such huge rock-like deposits of hard shells of diatoms constitute diatomaceous earth. Being gritty, the soil of diatomaceous earth. Being gritty, the soil of diatomaceous earth is used in polishing, filtration of oils and syrups. Diatoms are the chief 'producers' in the ocean.

80819.subject: Chemistry
80819.text: The correct formal charges on oxygen atoms numbered $2$, $1$ and $3$ respectively are :
80819.sol:
The formal charge (FC) on an atom in a Lewis structure is given by the formula:

$FC = V - L - \dfrac{S}{2}$

where $V$ is the number of valence electrons, $L$ is the number of non-bonding electrons, and $S$ is the number of shared (bonding) electrons.

For oxygen, the number of valence electrons is $V = 6$.

For oxygen atom $1$ (central atom):
It has $1$ lone pair ($2$ non-bonding electrons) and $3$ bonds ($6$ shared electrons).
$FC_{1} = 6 - 2 - \dfrac{6}{2} = +1$

For oxygen atom $2$ (left atom):
It has $2$ lone pairs ($4$ non-bonding electrons) and $2$ bonds ($4$ shared electrons).
$FC_{2} = 6 - 4 - \dfrac{4}{2} = 0$

For oxygen atom $3$ (right atom):
It has $3$ lone pairs ($6$ non-bonding electrons) and $1$ bond ($2$ shared electrons).
$FC_{3} = 6 - 6 - \dfrac{2}{2} = -1$

The formal charges on oxygen atoms numbered $2$, $1$, and $3$ respectively are $0, +1, -1$.

Answer: $0, +1, -1$

84106.subject: Zoology
84106.text: Which type of white blood cells are concerned with the release of histamine and the natural anticoagulant heparin?
84106.sol:
The basophils are probably like mast cells of connective tissue. They release heparin, histamine and serotonin. Their nucleus is usually three lobed and their granules take basic stain strongly.
Monocytes are largest of all types of leucocytes. Their mucleus is bean-shaped. They are motile and phagocytic in nature. They engulf bacteria and cellular debris. Generally, they will change into macrophages after entering tissue spaces. Eosinophils have two-lobed nucleus. They are non-phagocytic and help in dissolving blood clot. Their number increases in people with allergic conditions such as asthma or hay fever. Neutrophils are most numerous of all leucocytes. They eat harmful germs and are therefore, phagocytic in nature. Their nucleus is many lobed and stain weakly with both acid and basic stains.

84979.subject: Zoology
options: molecular analysis of profiles of DNA samples
analysis of DNA samples using imprinting devices
techniques used for molecular analysis of different specimens of DNA
techniques used for identification of fingerprints of individuals.
84979.sol:
DNA fingerprinting involves determining the genetic makeup of a person. Determining and analysing the repeated sequences (as in STR), form the basis of DNA fingerprinting.
Related Theory
Sir Alec Jeffreys is the father of DNA fingerprinting. DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) represents the blueprint of the human genetic makeup. A DNA fingerprint, therefore, is a DNA pattern that has a unique sequence such that it can be distinguished from the DNA patterns of other individuals. DNA fingerprinting is also called DNA typing.
Caution
Earlier, VNTRs (Variable Number Tandem Repeats) sequence were analysed during the process. However, with advancement of technology, STRs (Short Tandem Repeats) are studied present, which provide better results than VNTR.

88113.text:
A solution of Ni(NO3)2 is electrolyzed between platinum electrodes using a current of 5 amperes for 20 min. What mass of Ni is deposited at the cathode ? (Atomic mass of Ni = 58.7)
[Report your answer by rounding it upto nearset whole number]
88113.sol:
Quantity of electricity used = Current in amperes x Time in second = 5A x (20 x 60) s = 6000 C

Chemical equation for the reaction during electrolysis :

$\begin{cases}\text{Ni} {\left({\text{NO}}_{3}\right)}_{2} \left(\text{aq}\right) + 2 {\text{H}}^{+} & + & 2 {\text{e}}^{-} & ⟶ & \text{Ni} & + & 2 {\text{HNO}}_{3} \\ & & 2 \text{F} & & 5 8 \text{.} 7 \text{g} & & \end{cases}$

Charge Q on n moles of electrons is given by : Q = nF

Charge required to deposit 1 mole nickel

= 2 F = 2 x 96500 C = 1.93 x 105 C

Molar mass of nickel = 58.7g mol-1

1.93 x 105 C of charge produces nickel = 58.7g

6000 C of charge produces nickel $= \dfrac{\left(5 8 \text{.} 7 \text{g}\right) \times \left(6 0 0 0 \text{C}\right)}{\left(1 \text{.} 9 3 \times 1 {0}^{5} \text{C}\right)}$

$= 1 \text{.} 8 2\text{g}$

91645.text: Vipin and Shubham are playing a game with a coin, that comes up heads with a probability $p .$ They take turns flipping the coin until one of them wins, with Vipin going first. 91645.sol:
$P\left(H\right) = p, P\left(T\right) = 1 - p$
Probability of Vipin winning game is $P\left(H\right) + P\left(T\right)P\left(H\right)P\left(H\right) + P\left(T\right)P\left(H\right)P\left(T\right)P\left(H\right)P\left(H\right) + . . . . . . . \left(infiniteseries\right)$
$= \dfrac{P\left(H\right)}{1 - P\left(H\right)P ( T )} = \dfrac{p}{1 - p ( 1 - p )} = \dfrac{p}{1 - p + {p}^{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{p}{1 - p + {p}^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(given\right)$
$⇒ 2p = 1 - p + {p}^{2}$
$⇒ {p}^{2} - 3p + 1 = 0$

$⇒ p = \dfrac{3 \pm \sqrt{5}}{2}\left[∴ p = \dfrac{3 + \sqrt{5}}{2} > 1\right]$
$⇒ p = \dfrac{3 - \sqrt{5}}{2} = {\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{5} - 1}{4}\right)}^{2} \times 4 = 4\sin^{2}{162}^{o}$
$⇒ k = 4$

92702.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
92702.text: A tennis ball with (small) mass ${m}_{2}$, sits on the top of a basketball with (large) mass ${m}_{1}$. The bottom of the basketball is at a height $h$ above the ground and the bottom of the tennis ball is at a height $( h + d )$ above the ground. The balls are dropped from rest. Here all collisions are elastic and ${m}_{1} > > {m}_{2}$. The height from the point of collision up to which the tennis ball bounce is
92702.sol:
Just before the collision, the velocity of the basketball in the& downward direction is& $\sqrt{2gh}$ and just after the collision its velocity reverses its direction

So just& after the collision, the downward moving tennis ball collides with upward moving basketball. The velocity of the tennis ball after this collision is

$v = - \left(- 2\sqrt{2gh}\right) + \sqrt{2gh} ⇒ v = 3\sqrt{2gh}$

The height up to which the tennis ball will bounce is

$h^{'} = \dfrac{\left(3\sqrt{2gh}\right)2}{2g} ⇒ h^{'} = 9h$

92780.sol:
In the first case, the emf of the battery is

$E = {Kl}_{1}$, where $K$ is the potential gradient and& ${l}_{1}$ is the first balancing length.

In the second case the potential difference across the battery is

$\dfrac{ER}{\text{r} + \text{R}} = {Kl}_{2}$, where& $R$ is the shunt resistance used.

Dividing the above two equations, we get

$\dfrac{r}{R} + 1 = \dfrac{l1}{l2}$

$\text{⇒r} = 2\left[\dfrac{240 - 120}{120}\right] = 2Ω$

96280.text:
Match the processes occurs during cell cycle with the names of the events
&
$( P )$ Synapsis aligns homologous chromosomes (i) Anaphase-II
$( Q )$ Synthesis of RNA and protein (ii) Zygotene
$( R )$ Action of enzyme recombinase (iii) G-phase
$( S )$ Centromeres do not separate but chromatids move towards opposite poles (iv) Anaphase-I
& & (v) Pachytene
96280.sol: Zygotene is the second stage of Prophase I where the chromosomes start pairing together. This process is called synapsis and the paired chromosomes are known as homologous chromosomes. Pachytene is the stage where bivalent chromosomes clearly appear as tetrads and is characterized by the appearance of recombination nodules which function as the sites of crossing over between non-sister chromatids of the homologous chromosomes. Crossing over is the exchange of genetic material between two homologous chromosomes and is mediated by the enzyme called recombinase. The stage where sister chromatids remain associated but homologous chromosomes separate is called Anaphase I. During Anaphase II the sister chromatids move towards the opposite poles of the cell due to the simultaneous splitting of the centromere.

96507.text: Which of the following condition will inhibit decomposition?
96507.sol: Decomposition is largely an oxygen-requiring process. The rate of decomposition is controlled by chemical composition of detritus and climatic factors. In a particular climatic condition, decomposition rate is slower if detritus is rich in lignin and chitin, and quicker, if detritus is rich in nitrogen and water-soluble substances like sugars. Temperature and soil moisture are the most important climatic factors that regulate decomposition through their effects on the activities of soil microbes. Warm and moist environment favour decomposition whereas low temperature and anaerobiosis inhibit decomposition resulting in buildup of organic materials.

100995.subject: Physics
100995.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
100995.text:
Statement-I: Two particles moving in the same direction do not lose all their energy in a completely inelastic collision.
Statement-II: Principle of conservation of momentum holds true for all kinds of collisions.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are incorrect.
Statement-I is correct and Statement-II is incorrect.
Statement-I is incorrect and Statement-II is correct.
100995.sol:
Let masses \(m_1, m_2\) have initial velocities \(u_1, u_2\) in the same direction and they stick after collision (perfectly, inelastic). Common velocity
\(v=$\frac{m_1 u_1+m_2 u_2}{m_1+m_2}$\)
Initial KE:
\(K_i=$\frac{1}{2}$m_1 u_1^2+$\frac{1}{2}$m_2 u_2^2,\)
Final KE:
\(K_f=$\frac{1}{2}\left($m_1+m_2\right) v²\)
Loss of kinetic energy
\($\Delta$K=K_i-K_f=$\frac{1}{2} \frac{m_1 m_2}{m_1+m_2}\left($u_1-u_2\right)^2 \geq 0\)
This loss is not the whole initial energy except when \(u_1=u_2\) (then \($\Delta$K=0\)). So Statement-1 is true: they do not lose all their energy in general.
Statement-II is also true: momentum is conserved in all collisions provided the system is isolated (no externa impulse). That includes elastic, inelastic, perfectly inelastic collisions and explosions (internal forces only).
So both are true \( → \) option (1).

102410.subject: Physics
102410.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): When a car accelerates horizontally, the tension in the string of a suspended pendulum in equilibrium (relative to the car) is greater than its actual weight ($mg$).
Reason (R): The effective acceleration due to gravity in the frame of the accelerating car is $\sqrt{g^2 + a^2}$, which is greater than $g$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
102410.sol:
In the frame of the accelerating car, the pendulum bob experiences a horizontal pseudo force $ma$ in the direction opposite to the acceleration, in addition to the downward gravitational force $mg$.

The net force acting on the bob in this non-inertial frame is $F_{\text{net}} = \sqrt{(mg)^2 + (ma)^2} = m\sqrt{g^2 + a^2}$.

Therefore, the effective acceleration due to gravity is $g_{\text{eff}} = \sqrt{g^2 + a^2}$, which is strictly greater than $g$.

To maintain equilibrium relative to the car, the tension $T$ in the string must balance this net force. Thus, $T = mg_{\text{eff}} = m\sqrt{g^2 + a^2}$.

Since $g_{\text{eff}} > g$, the tension $T$ is greater than the actual weight $mg$. Both the Assertion and Reason are true, and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
